It is not a situation where you have an indictment, which occurs in some cases, where there are different offences and, for some reason, the Prosecution can arguably put them all together in the one indictment, but they are, in fact, a series of separate and different offences against separate and different individuals. We have, in Count 1, a joint count. In my submission, for all of those reasons, this motion should be denied, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: May I, Your Honour? With regards to the Prosecution's position likening this to a jury trial and that the problem can be taken care of by a curative charge, I think that the Prosecution misunderstands the basic problem. The basic problem is not a curative charge; the basic problem is that there are statements which are inimical to my client which will be introduced into evidence, and if the defendants do not testify, I will lose the right to confrontation and cross-examination. With regard to the Prosecution's concern about my client and speedy trial, that is my concern, as my client's attorney, and I have spoken to my client, and I do not believe that that is a concern of the Prosecution unless I, on behalf of my client, would raise it. Finally, with regard to costs, I don't think justice has a price.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) My question relates to what we heard from the attorneys appearing as Defence counsel for the other accused, Mr. Pisarevic, Mr. Avramovic, Mr. Pantelic. You told us that the fact that we have a joint trial, if I noted it well, what Mr. Pisarevic said, could have an adverse effect on your client. Mr. Pisarevic I think was the one who said that, that this joint trial could have a negative effect on his client, and I think that this was confirmed by the other attorneys. So my first question is addressed to Mr. Pisarevic. Which negative implications do you fear this could have on your client, the fact that we have a joint trial for all the accused? My second question is to Mr. Pantelic. You elaborated on the question of expediency during the Status Conference. I think you made that point last week and I think we understand one another, so we need not go back to it. So the question is: What are the negative effects of a joint trial on the other accused? That is my question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. President, Your Honours, allow me to answer that question. Let me try and explain the negative effects that my client could suffer and that could put him in an unfavourable position. First of all, my client, as I have said, has been charged with quite different criminal offences compared to those that Mr. Todorovic is charged with, and I think that in the course of such a trial, what could happen could be that the whole trial, in terms of its significance, weight, and the testimony of all the witnesses that might appear, could be shifted to establishing the facts which are of greatest significance regarding the case against Mr. Todorovic than against the other accused. This is a circumstance which has certain consequences for each individual because Mr. Zaric, as the fourth accused, will not be able sufficiently to bring home his own arguments and positions and make the best of the witness statements. Another adverse effect could be that the preparations for Mr. Todorovic, for his defence, requires more time, and we appreciate that, and as Mr. Zaric has been here for more than a year already, we feel that Mr. Todorovic's defence preparations could postpone or delay the whole proceedings. Many witnesses who have been called by the Prosecution could not be used as witnesses in the case against Mr. Zaric and in the case against Mr. Todorovic. All this, the duration of the proceedings, et cetera, could have a negative effect on Mr. Zaric and the other co-accused who would have to go through this whole procedure of examination of witnesses and cross-examination of witnesses which will probably be large in number, and I think by severing the trial, the proceedings which they, of course, will have to live through would be easier to live through by the accused, and I think in that case, one could, with greater certainty, ensure respect of the rights of Mr. Zaric and the other accused and that this would contribute to the course of justice. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We will consider this motion and give our ruling in due course. It's now five past five, and it would be simplest, I think, if we rose in order that the Status Conference could be prepared. Two of us will return for that, and we hope very much that we can finish before half past five.
